answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 8 times its size, so a group of 82 keys loses far more than 82 single identities would. The umber graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the timber audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the juniper checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
